subject: Limited indemnity for MVP order form — proposed compromise
messages:

Subject: Limited indemnity for Redwood Order Form (MVP)

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the product looks promising. Procurement has a couple of hard lines on indemnity we need to resolve before we can move to PO:

- Biosync cannot accept a broad customer indemnity for IP claims tied to output of the model. We need Redwood to defend and indemnify for third-party IP infringement that results from Redwood-provided model weights/code.
- Our standard cap for third-party IP is $1.0M aggregate; we cannot accept unlimited liability or a cap tied only to annual fees unless we have additional remedies.
- We also require reasonable notice timelines (30 days), cooperation on defense, and an option to control settlement if material.

Can Redwood provide revised redlines that narrow the customer indemnity and include an insurance offset clause (we typically require proof of insurance as well)? I attached our procurement checklist for reference (Biosync_Procurement_Requirements.pdf).

If you can get us a proposed compromise by EOD Tuesday we can escalate to legal here.

Thanks,
Elaine

Subject: Re: Limited indemnity for Redwood Order Form (MVP)

Elaine — thanks for the clear summary and the checklist. We've reviewed and put together a pragmatic compromise that should address Biosync's concerns while preserving standard protections for Redwood. High level:

- Mutual IP indemnity for infringement of third-party IP arising from the other party's intellectual property (code, model weights, documentation).
- For customer use of model outputs: Redwood will indemnify Biosync only where a third-party claim alleges infringement by Redwood's supplied model or prepackaged deliverables; Redwood will not be responsible for claims arising solely from Biosync's prompt engineering, user-provided content, or downstream modifications.
- Liability cap for IP indemnity: Redwood proposes a $1,000,000 cap for third-party IP defense/indemnity (aggregate) for the MVP order form.
- Defense control: Redwood will offer to assume defense with counsel of Redwood's choosing; Biosync can request substitution if reasonable conflict arises. We propose a cooperation and notice obligation (notice within 30 days of becoming aware).
- Insurance offset: Redwood requests the right to offset indemnity by any insurance proceeds actually received by the indemnitee (standard insurance offset).

Attached: Redwood_OrderForm_MVP_v3_redlines.pdf with tracked changes and a short doc (Redwood_IP-Definition-Proposed.txt) that tightens the definition of "IP Claim" to focus on code/weights/documentation we ship.

Ben (cc'd) will follow up on the commercial cap math and any potential credit/discount trade if Biosync needs a higher cap. Kimberly and I are available for a short call with Tom if legal wants to walk through the redlines.

Would that be sufficient to get procurement comfortable?

Best,

Subject: INTERNAL: suggested legal redlines for Biosync — language to send

Team — drafting suggestions to make Priya's compromise legally robust. Below is the language I suggest we include in the Order Form / MSA redlines. Please treat as internal draft; I'll sign off before we send externally.

1) Narrow "IP Claim" definition
Proposed insertion (text to include in defined terms):
""IP Claim" means any claim, demand, or suit by a third party that the unmodified Software, model weights, or documentation provided by Redwood infringes that third party's valid patent, copyright, or trademark rights. IP Claim does not include claims based on (a) Customer Data, (b) Customer-provided prompts or instructions, or (c) outputs generated by the model that are subsequently modified by Customer or Users.""

2) Defense and control
- Redwood may assume defense of an IP Claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to Customer; Customer shall cooperate and provide information reasonably requested. Redwood will not settle any claim that admits liability or imposes injunctive relief on Customer without Customer's written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).

3) Cap and insurance offset
- For IP Claims, Redwood's aggregate liability shall not exceed $1,000,000.
- Any indemnity payment shall be reduced by insurance proceeds actually recovered by the indemnified party.

4) Prompt notice and mitigation
- Customer must notify Redwood within 30 days of receipt of written notice of an IP Claim. Failure to timely notify does not relieve Redwood except to the extent Redwood is prejudiced.

5) Remedy substitution / replacement option
- If an injunction of the Software or model is sought, Redwood may, at its option, (a) procure the right to continue Customer's use, (b) replace or modify the Software or model to make it non-infringing, or (c) if neither is commercially feasible, terminate the affected service and refund prepaid fees for the affected portion.

Comments: the replacement/termination remedies are critical for Biosync's operational continuity. The proposed cap ($1M) aligns with their ask and our current MVP risk appetite. We should prepare a short one-page explainer for procurement showing the trade (cap + remedial options vs unlimited).

I will incorporate the redline text into the PDF Priya attached and send a clean version to Elaine once Ben confirms the commercial trade.

-Kim

Priya / Kim — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear language. The redlines look reasonable and Biosync legal is aligned on the carveouts for customer-modified outputs. A few small asks before we sign:

- Can we get a statement of Redwood's cyber/tech insurance limits and the carrier? We need the insurer name and limits for our vendor risk team.
- Please add explicit language that Redwood's remedial substitution (replace/modify) will be pursued in good faith and on a commercially reasonable basis — we can accept your three-option ladder so long as that qualifier is present.
- Evidence timing: if we get a claim we may need certain technical artifacts (model version, inference logs for a 30-day window). Can Redwood commit to producing those within 7 business days on written request (subject to reasonable redaction)?

If those items are accommodated in the final redline we can issue the PO and loop in Finance for payment. Appreciate the collaborative approach — looking forward to getting this closed.

Best,
Elaine
